lines.say: 59.6k stars, for a framework that turns plain HTML into finished video.
It's called HyperFrames, and it comes from HeyGen. You write HTML, and it renders video. It was built for agents.
You define the whole video as an HTML page. Data attributes on each element set when it starts and how long it plays.
Under the hood, it drives headless Chrome, captures every frame, encodes the video, and mixes the audio.
Unlike Remotion, there is no build step. Your index.html plays exactly as it is.
It ships 21 skills that coding agents load on demand, from product launch videos to captions for a talking head.
A catalog adds ready-made blocks for transitions, overlays, captions and animated charts.
It is used in production at HeyGen, with community examples from teams like tldraw and TanStack.
To start, you need Node.js 22 or newer and FFmpeg. Run npx hyperframes init, then preview, then render to MP4.
Or install the plugin in Claude Code, and simply ask your agent for the video you want.
Send this to someone who still edits every video by hand.
HyperFrames, by HeyGen. Write HTML, render video.
